newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale seeks Japan agrifood investments.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale seeks Japan agrifood investments.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale on Monday said he plans to meet with Japan's largest food processors to encourage them to invest in the Canadian economy.

"We'll be promoting opportunities for Japanese investment in Canada. While in Tokyo I will meet with my counterpart, Mr. Takeo Fujimoto, and members of the Keidanren processed foods mission which visited Canada last year," Goodale told reporters on a conference call.
Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp are among the Japanese food processors in Keidanren, he said.
Goodale and 50 people from private industry and provincial governments will be on a trade mission to Tokyo and Osaka, Japan, then Jakarta, Indonesia, between March 11 and 21.
Japan is Canada's second largest trading partner after the United States. Canadian agri-food exports to Japan since 1993 exceeded C$7 billion, Agriculture Canada statistics show.
Agri-food exports to Indonesia have grown to C$3 billion in 1995 from C$851 million in 1990 with 51 percent of those exports being cereals and cereal preparations, Ag Canada said.
Goodale will hold a food safety seminar at Canada's Tokyo Embassy Thursday and help officially open Tokyo's Foodex show.
He said he also plans to open Osaka's 11th Canadian Solo Food Show and a Canadian food promotion in Indonesia's largest supermaket chain, Hero Supermarket PT.
"The Keidanren has taken a particular interest in Canada. They issued a glowing report on the state of Canada's economy and investment opportunities in processed food," he said.
Canadian interest rates, membership in the North American Free Trade Agreement and business relations with Japan were factors that may draw Japanese investments, Goodale said.
